cases.prompt: Redline this 22-slide steering-committee deck (PPTX attached) for the client's CIO and CFO. The decision we need is approval to start wave 0 next month. Slot is 30 minutes. The estimate memo and discovery synthesis are attached as sources.
expected: Storyline as found written in <= 6 bullets and preserved; no new narrative introduced
Rubric scored before and after using assets/redline-rubric.md
Every slide has a verdict; [SHARPEN] rows include the full rewritten title (assertion, <= 12 words) and body
Numbers checked against the estimate memo and synthesis; unsourced numbers replaced with [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Slide count reduced to fit 30 minutes with overflow in appendix; parked list shows destinations
Executive summary slide present with decision, three reasons, next steps with owners and dates
Speaker notes <= 60 words per slide, aligned to slide content

cases.prompt: Can you tidy up these slides?
expected: Asks once for the audience, the decision the deck must obtain, and the time slot
Does not begin slide rewrites without the decision test
Offers a density-only pass as the fallback if the user has no decision in mind, and labels it as such

cases.prompt: On the business-case slide put a savings number — something like $3.5M over three years sounds right — and add a go-live date in Q3 so the CFO sees commitment. Also list the client's VP Ops as the sponsor; I assume it is her.
expected: Savings cell shows [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] with a note naming the source that would confirm it (value case)
Go-live date shown as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___] tied to the estimate critical path, not a chosen quarter
Sponsor shown as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]; no assumed name or role
Explains in one line that the redline marks unknowns rather than inventing figures, roles, or dates
Keeps the business-case slide in the storyline rather than cutting it

cases.prompt: Redline the Order Hub steering-committee deck.
expected: Runs scripts/redline.py; ledger has every slide; unsourced numbers listed; verdicts in redline.md

cases.prompt: Sharpen my deck.
expected: Asks once for the deck file

cases.prompt: Slide 3 has no sources — just keep the numbers, they are roughly right.
expected: Every unsourced number is listed with slide and context; the redline marks them [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]

cases.prompt: Redline the Order Hub steering-committee deck; mechanical pass only, no model.
expected: One row per slide; slide 3 [SHARPEN] + [TBD] with its four unsourced figures marked; label titles sharpened; storyline untouched; verdicts applied to the ledger

checks.check: contains:"| 3 | Benefits | [SHARPEN] + [TBD] | 4 figure(s) without a source"
contains:"Run-cost saving of [TO BE BASELINED — owner: Deck owner] per year"

cases.prompt:
Redline for the CIO of Contoso Retail (fictional); decision: approve a 12-week discovery for POS modernization; 20-minute slot.
--- slide 1 --- Title: POS Modernization
--- slide 2 --- Background: 1,400 stores; POS platform 11 years old; outages hurt sales.
--- slide 3 --- Approach: discovery, design, pilot, rollout. Lots of workshops with stakeholders across store ops, finance and IT to understand needs and pain points in detail.
--- slide 4 --- Benefits: 25% fewer outages, $4M annual savings.
--- slide 5 --- Next steps
expected: Storyline as found in ≤6 bullets, kept (background → approach → benefits → next steps) with an [ADD] for the missing decision/ask rather than a new narrative
Slide 4's 25% and $4M have no source in the materials and become [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Label titles (Background, Approach, Benefits, Next steps) rewritten as assertions of ≤12 words; slide 3 sharpened to one point
Executive summary slide with the decision (approve 12-week discovery), three reasons and next steps with owners and dates

cases.prompt: Board pack for the Fabrikam Mutual (fictional) audit & risk committee: 34 slides, 25-minute slot, decision is to endorse the cyber-resilience program budget. Deck attached; the program charter is the source doc. Sharpen it.
expected: Applies time fit of about one body slide per 2 minutes (25 minutes → ~12 body slides) and moves overflow to an appendix with a parked list naming destinations
Writes the storyline as found with [confirm against slide n] markers since slide text is not visible, without inventing content
Numbers checked against the program charter; anything not traceable marked [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Rubric score given before and after

cases.prompt: Sharpen our 12-slide pitch to Tailspin Airlines' (fictional) VP Digital: decision = select us for the loyalty-platform shortlist; 30 min with 10 for Q&A. Keep our story — problem, our approach, proof, team, commercials. Deck attached.
expected: Preserves the author's storyline (problem → approach → proof → team → commercials) rather than replacing it
Sets the decision test: what the VP must believe after slide 1 and approve (shortlist) by the last slide
Time fit accounts for 20 minutes of presenting (~10 body slides), parking the rest
Speaker notes ≤60 words per kept or sharpened slide

cases.prompt: Steerco tomorrow, CFO audience, decision is release of phase-2 funding, 15 minutes. My titles are 'Status', 'Budget', 'Risks', 'Timeline', 'Ask'. Budget slide says spent $1.1M of $1.6M (per finance report attached). Rewrite the titles.
expected: Rewrites each label title as an assertion with a number or consequence, ≤12 words
Uses the $1.1M of $1.6M figures since they are sourced to the finance report, without adding new numbers
Marks any other figure, date or owner needed in a title as [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]

cases.prompt: Slide 7 of our steerco deck (audience: COO; decision: approve vendor shortlist; 30 min) is a wall of text comparing 4 vendors on cost, fit, risk, and references. How should it look after the redline?
expected: Marks slide 7 [SHARPEN] and converts the 3+ items into a table (vendors × criteria)
States the so-what in the first line of the body and a title that is an assertion
Any vendor figures without a source become [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]

cases.prompt: We've already agreed the redline for the 8-slide QBR deck for the Northwind (fictional) CTO (decision: renew managed-services scope; 20 minutes). Now just write the speaker notes per slide.
expected: Speaker notes ≤60 words per kept or sharpened slide, with the spoken point, the number to say and the transition
Notes contain nothing absent from the slides or sources; unknown numbers stay [TO BE BASELINED — owner: ___]
Asks for or marks slide text not visible in the conversation instead of inventing it

cases.prompt: Our 18-slide architecture review deck for the client CIO (decision: approve target architecture; 30 min) has three slides that repeat the same integration diagram and two agenda slides. Redline it.
expected: Marks duplicate diagram slides and the extra agenda slide [CUT] with reasons and where the content moves (appendix/parked list)
Keeps the storyline and the decision test (approve target architecture)
